Based on Ta’lim al-Sibyan al-Tawhid by Shaykh Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab, and its companion poem (Manẓūmah), as taught across the 9 lessons of the AMAN Tawḥīd curriculum. Every question is built from the same proofs, definitions, and wording used in class.

Al-Madrasatu An-Nuriyyah (AMAN)
Tawhid Study Guide 1
Lesson 0 · Introduction
SG 1
Hides every gold word and answer so you can quiz yourself — click any hidden box to reveal it.
Assessed in:CW 1HW 1QZ 1TS 1TS 6EX 1EX 2
Tawḥīd comes first. The poem opens by saying nothing at all benefits a person without it — so everything else in the deen is built on it. The class goal is to become a مُوَحِّدٌ جَيِّد: someone who worships Allah alone and understands why, with proof.
Key Terms
التَّوْحِيدWorshipping Allah alone, with no partner
الدَّلِيلThe proof (an ayah or hadith) behind an answer
الْفِطْرَةThe natural disposition every person is born with, inclined toward Allah
مُوَحِّدOne who worships Allah alone, with understanding
الْمُوَحِّدُ الْجَيِّد“A good Muwahhid” — knows why he worships Allah alone, and the proof
السِّبْيَانChildren / young boys (in the book’s title)
Must-Know Facts
  • The unit is based on the book Ta’līm aṣ-Ṣibyān at-Tawḥīd by Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab. The poem (naẓm) is the same book in verse.
  • The poem exists so the content can be memorized more easily.
  • Every answer in the book is given with a dalīl (Qur’an or ḥadīth proof).
  • Al-Fiṭrah is natural — it is not a belief taught from scratch.
  • The goal is understanding — not repeating answers without knowing the dalīl behind them.

Watch Out — Common Mistakes

Tawhid Study Guide 2
Lesson 1 · Q1–Q2 — Who is your Lord?
SG 2
Hides every gold word and answer so you can quiz yourself — click any hidden box to reveal it.
Assessed in:CW 2HW 2QZ 2TS 1TS 6EX 1
Q1: مَنْ رَبُّكَ؟ — رَبِّيَ اللَّهُ. “Rabb” carries six meanings. The Name “Allah” points to something specific: His unique right to be worshipped (Ulūhiyyah).
Key Terms
الْخَالِقCreator
الْمَالِكOwner
الرَّازِقProvider
الْمُعِينHelper
النَّاصِرSupporter
الْمَعْبُودThe One Worshipped
اللَّهThe One possessing Ulūhiyyah, deserving worship from ALL creation
الأُلُوهِيَّةThe quality of truly deserving worship
الْعُبُودِيَّةComplete servitude to Allah
Must-Know Facts
  • Ar-Rabb has six meanings — Creator, Owner, Provider, Helper, Supporter, and the One Worshipped. It does not have just one.
  • Rabb points to Allah’s lordship and His actions. Allah points to His unique right to be worshipped. They are not exact synonyms.
  • Al-Ulūhiyyah is the quality of deserving worship — not merely creating.
  • One proof — Al-A‘rāf 7:54 — answers Q1, Q2 and Q3 together.
  • الشَّهِيد (Witness) is not one of the six meanings.
Proofs (Dalīl)
Al-A‘rāf 7:54
Answers Q1, Q2 and Q3 together — heavens and earth created in six days.

Tawhid Study Guide 3
Lesson 2 · Q3 — His Signs
SG 3
Hides every gold word and answer so you can quiz yourself — click any hidden box to reveal it.
Assessed in:CW 3HW 3QZ 3TS 1TS 6
Q3: بِمَ تَعْرِفُ رَبَّكَ؟ — we know our Lord through His signs (āyāt) and His creation. Knowing Him this way should lead to gratitude, remembrance and worship.
Key Terms
الْآيَاتSigns of Allah
الأَرْضThe earth
السَّمَاءThe sky
الشَّمْسThe sun
الْبَدْرThe moon
السَّاعَاتThe passing hours
Must-Know Facts
  • A sign is what Allah alone does — the sun, moon, earth, sky. Man-made things (a drawing, video game, toy, cartoon) are not signs of Allah.
  • The poem lists five signs: the earth, the sky, the sun, the moon, and the passing hours. Night and day changing is also a sign.
  • Signs are found in creation itself — not only in the Qur’an’s text. The Qur’an describes creation as a proof pointing to the Creator.
  • We do not know Allah only because someone told us — His signs show Him too.
  • Why it matters: it should lead to gratitude, remembrance (dhikr) and worship — not taking creation for granted.
Proofs (Dalīl)
Al-A‘rāf 7:54
Answers Q1, Q2 and Q3 together — heavens and earth created in six days.

Tawhid Study Guide 4
Lesson 3 · Q4 — Purpose & Ibadah
SG 4
Hides every gold word and answer so you can quiz yourself — click any hidden box to reveal it.
Assessed in:CW 4HW 4QZ 4TS 2TS 6
Q4: لِأَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَكَ اللَّهُ؟ — to worship Him alone, with no partner. Worship is only accepted with both conditions: sincerity (Ikhlāṣ) and following the Prophet ﷺ (Mutāba‘ah).
Key Terms
الْعِبَادَةEverything Allah loves and is pleased with — inward and outward, words and actions
إِخْلَاصSincerity — worship for Allah alone
اتِّبَاعFollowing the Prophet ﷺ (Mutāba‘ah)
رِيَاءShowing off — doing worship to be seen by people
Must-Know Facts
  • The purpose of creation is worship of Allah alone.
  • Q4 has two proofs: Adh-Dhāriyāt 51:56 and An-Nisā’ 4:36. (Al-Ikhlāṣ 112:1 is not one of them.)
  • Ibādah is a comprehensive term for everything Allah loves and is pleased with — far more than the five prayers. This definition is credited to Ibn Taymiyyah.
  • Two conditions for accepted worship — Ikhlāṣ and Mutāba‘ah. A deed needs both together; looking correct outwardly is not enough.
  • Riyā’ ruins sincerity — the deed is no longer purely for Allah, so it can be rejected.
Proofs (Dalīl)
Adh-Dhāriyāt 51:56
“I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Me.”
An-Nisā’ 4:36
Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him.

Tawhid Study Guide 5
Lesson 4 · Shirk — Definitions & Proofs
SG 5
Hides every gold word and answer so you can quiz yourself — click any hidden box to reveal it.
Assessed in:CW 5CW 6HW 5HW 6QZ 5TS 2TS 6EX 1
Shirk is making a نِدّ (a rival) for Allah in worship — directing worship to a created being. It is the greatest of all sins, and it forbids Jannah.
Key Terms
الشِّرْكMaking a rival for Allah in worship
نِدّA rival
مَخْلُوقA creation / created being
الدُّعَاءCalling on / asking — “the marrow of worship” (مُخُّ الْعِبَادَة)
الْخَوْفFear
الرَّجَاءHope
التَّوَكُّلReliance
الْمَحَبَّةLove / desire
Must-Know Facts
  • Shirk = making a nidd for Allah — calling on it, hoping in it, fearing it, relying on it, or having strong desire toward it, besides Allah.
  • Five types of worship where Shirk can occur: Du‘ā, Khawf, Rajā’, Tawakkul, Mahabbah. (Ṣalāh is not on this list.)
  • Khawf becomes Shirk if directed to other than Allah in a controlling way. Rajā’: hoping in a creation the way one hopes in Allah. Tawakkul: relying totally on other than Allah.
  • Full trust in Allah while using permitted means (like studying for a test) is correct Tawakkul — not Shirk.
  • Shirk is the greatest of all sins — not a minor or easily forgivable one.
Proofs (Dalīl)
Al-Mā’idah 5:72
Shirk forbids Jannah; one’s home becomes the Fire.
Al-Jinn 72:18
Mosques are for Allah — do not call on anyone besides Him.
Al-Mu’minūn 23:117
Du‘ā to another deity = Kufr. Such a person will NOT succeed (لَا يُفْلِحُ الْكَافِرُونَ).
Ghāfir 40:60
Du‘ā IS an act of worship.
Az-Zumar 39:64-66
Shirk nullifies ALL good deeds — even hypothetically warning the Prophet ﷺ.

Watch Out — Common Mistakes

Tawhid Study Guide 6
Lesson 5 · Taghut — Definition & the First Obligation
SG 6
Hides every gold word and answer so you can quiz yourself — click any hidden box to reveal it.
Assessed in:CW 7CW 8HW 7HW 8QZ 6TS 3TS 7
Ṭāghūt is whatever a servant goes beyond his proper limit with — something worshipped, followed, or obeyed besides Allah. The first obligation is الْكُفْرُ بِالطَّاغُوتِ وَالإِيمَانُ بِاللَّهِ — reject what is false first, then affirm Allah.
Key Terms
الطَّاغُوتWhat the servant crosses his proper limit with — worshipped, followed or obeyed besides Allah
حَدّLimit
الْكُفْر بِالطَّاغُوتRejecting Ṭāghūt
الكَاهِنSoothsayer — claims knowledge of the unseen
الْمُنَجِّمAstrologer — uses the stars to predict the future
لَا إِلَهَ — إِلَّا اللَّهNegation first, then affirmation
Must-Know Facts
  • The definition of Ṭāghūt taught in class is credited to Ibn al-Qayyim. Three categories: something worshipped, followed, or obeyed besides Allah.
  • First obligation on every servant: kufr bi-Ṭāghūt and īmān billāh. Rejecting Ṭāghūt is obligatory for every believer — never optional.
  • An-Naḥl 16:36: every messenger to every nation called: worship Allah and avoid Ṭāghūt.
  • Lā ilāha illa Allāh negates everything false FIRST (لَا إِلَهَ), then affirms Allah (إِلَّا اللَّه) — the same order as kufr bi-Ṭāghūt before īmān billāh.
  • Examples: a Kāhin, a Munajjim, someone obeyed while commanding disobedience to Allah. Modern: horoscopes/fortune-telling, a person or ideology obeyed even in sin, wealth or fame treated as life’s ultimate purpose.
  • Consulting a fortune-teller “just to check” is forbidden and undermines correct worship. A person cannot be a complete believer while following a Ṭāghūt.
Proofs (Dalīl)
An-Naḥl 16:36
Every messenger to every nation: worship Allah and avoid Taghut.

Tawhid Study Guide 7
Lesson 6 · Q5 — Islam & the Five Pillars
SG 7
Hides every gold word and answer so you can quiz yourself — click any hidden box to reveal it.
Assessed in:CW 9HW 9QZ 7TS 3TS 4TS 7
Q5: مَا دِينُكَ؟ — دِينِيَ الإِسْلَامُ. Islam has four components and five pillars. Belief alone is not enough.
Key Terms
الإِسْلَامThe religion accepted by Allah
الِاسْتِسْلَامSubmission to Allah through Tawḥīd
الْمُوَالَاةAllegiance toward Muslims (muwālāh)
مُعَادَاةُ الْمُشْرِكِينَRejecting Shirk and its people (mu‘ādāh)
الشَّهَادَتَانThe two testimonies
الصَّلَاةPrayer
الزَّكَاةZakah
الصَّوْمFasting
الْحَجّHajj
Must-Know Facts
  • Four components of Islam: (1) submission through Tawḥīd, (2) compliance through obedience, (3) allegiance toward Muslims, (4) rejection of Shirk and its people.
  • Why belief alone is not enough: Islam also requires actual obedience, loyalty to fellow believers, and active rejection of Shirk.
  • Five pillars: Shahādatayn, Ṣalāh, Zakah, Ṣawm, Ḥajj. Zakah is a pillar. Jihad is not one of the five.
  • Hajj is obligatory only on those who are able (physically and financially).
  • Islam is the religion of Allah for ALL His servants — not only Arabs — from the creation of Ādam on.
Proofs (Dalīl)
Āl-‘Imrān 3:19
The religion accepted by Allah is Islam.
Āl-‘Imrān 3:85
Seeking a religion other than Islam is never accepted.
Al-Bayyinah 98:5
Proof for the first three pillars (Shahādatayn, Ṣalāh, Zakah).
Al-Baqarah 2:183
Proof that fasting is obligatory.
Āl-‘Imrān 3:97
Proof for Hajj — on those who are able.

Tawhid Study Guide 8
Lesson 6 · Īmān & the Unseen
SG 8
Hides every gold word and answer so you can quiz yourself — click any hidden box to reveal it.
Assessed in:CW 10HW 10QZ 8TS 4TS 7
Īmān has six pillars, and all six must be believed in together. Denying the resurrection is Kufr — the poem places the one who denies it in the Fire forever.
Key Terms
الْإِيمَانFaith — the six pillars
الْبَعْثResurrection — coming back to life after death
الْحِسَابThe Reckoning — full accounting of every deed
الْجَزَاءReward or punishment based on deeds
الْقَدَرAllah’s decree — good and difficult
الْكُتُبThe Books
Must-Know Facts
  • The six pillars of Īmān: Allah, the Angels, the Books, the Messengers, the Last Day, and Al-Qadar.
  • All six must be believed in together — a person cannot pick and choose. The Five Pillars of Islam are not one of the six.
  • A believer must accept Al-Qadar in both the good and the difficult decree. In the poem, وَالَّذِي كُتِبْ refers to Al-Qadar.
  • Al-Ba‘th is coming back to life after death. Denying it is Kufr — it is one of the six pillars, a foundation, not optional.
  • After being raised, people face Jannah, the Fire, and al-Ḥisāb.
Proofs (Dalīl)
Ar-Ra‘d 13:5
Calls denial of the resurrection an astonishing statement.

SG 9

Q6: مَنْ نَبِيُّكَ؟ — answered with his full five-name lineage. He ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets, sent to all of humanity.
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ بْنِ عَبْدِ مَنَافٍ ﷺ
The Prophet’s ﷺ Life at a Glance
Age 40Revelation begins
13 yearsCalling in Makkah (3 in secret)
Isrā’ & Mi‘rājFive prayers made obligatory — before the Hijrah
HijrahTo Madinah
10 yearsIn Madinah
Age 63Passes away · 23 years in total
Key Terms
خَاتَمُ النَّبِيِّينSeal (last) of the Prophets
اصْطِفَاءAllah’s deliberate selection of Muhammad ﷺ
الأَحْمَر وَالأَسْوَدIdiom: all of humanity
الصَّحَابَةThe Companions — best generation after the prophets
التَّابِعُونThe Followers — the generation after the Ṣaḥābah
الْأَتْبَاعThe Followers of the Followers — the generation after them
Must-Know Facts
  • Lineage: Muhammad ibn ‘Abdillah ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hāshim ibn ‘Abd Manāf ﷺ. Proof that he is the Seal: Al-Aḥzāb 33:40.
  • He ﷺ was sent to ALL of humanity (الأَحْمَر وَالأَسْوَد), not only the Arabs. There is no prophet after him.
  • Revelation began at 40. He called for 23 years total: 13 in Makkah (3 in secret) and 10 in Madinah. He passed away at 63, after the religion was completed and perfected.
  • The Isrā’ and Mi‘rāj happened before the Hijrah, still in Makkah — the five daily prayers were made obligatory then.
  • Nūḥ was the first messenger (after Shirk appeared). Muhammad ﷺ is the last in time but first in rank.
  • The four rightly-guided caliphs, in order: Abū Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Uthmān, ‘Alī.
  • Best generations: the Ṣaḥābah, then the Tābi‘ūn, then the Followers of the Followers.
  • ‘Eesā will descend near the end of time, break the cross, the swine will be killed — and mankind will accept ONLY Islam.

وَبَعْدَهَا الْهِجْرَةُ لِلْمَدِينَةْ عَشْرًا بِهَا أَقَامَ مِنْ سِنِينَةْThen the Hijrah to Madinah, where he stayed ten years.
ثَلَاثَةٌ زَادَتْ عَلَى السِّتِّينَا مُبَلِّغًا بَلَاغَهُ الْمُبِينَاThree years beyond sixty — conveying the clear message.
وَأَوَّلُ الرُّسْلِ الْكِرَامِ نُوحُ بَعْدَ ظُهُورِ الشِّرْكِ جَاءَ الرُّوحُThe first of the noble messengers is Nuh, after Shirk had appeared.
آخِرُهُمْ مُحَمَّدٌ زَمَانَا لَكِنَّهُ أَوَّلُهُمْ مَكَانَاThe last of them in time was Muhammad — but he is the first of them in rank.
أَوَّلُهُمْ صِدِّيقُهُمْ ثُمَّ عُمَرْ عُثْمَانُ بَعْدُ وَعَلِيٌّ مُعْتَبَرْThe four caliphs in order: Abu Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Uthman, ‘Ali.
وَأَفْضَلُ النَّاسِ بَعْدَ الْأَنْبِيَا أَصْحَابُهُ خَيْرُ الْقُرُونِ عَالِيَا
وَخَيْرُ قَرْنٍ بَعْدَهُمُ الَاتْبَاعُ فَتَبَعُ الْأَتْبَاعِ يَا شُجَاعُ
وَآخِرَ الزَّمَانِ عِيسَى يَنْزِلُ فَيُدْرِكُ الدَّجَّالَ ثُمَّ يَقْتُلُ
وَيَقْبَلُ الْإِسْلَامَ لَا سِوَاهُ تَمَّ وَحَمْدُ اللَّهِ مُنْتَهَاهُAfter ‘Eesa’s return, mankind will accept ONLY Islam.

Tawhid Study Guide 9 · Lesson 7 · Q6 — The Prophet ﷺ — page 3 of 3
Watch Out — Common Mistakes
Khātam an-Nabiyyīn means the first of the prophets.
It means the Seal (last) of the prophets.
The Prophet ﷺ was sent only to the Arabs.
He ﷺ was sent to all of humanity.
The Isrā’ and Mi‘rāj happened after the Hijrah.
They happened before the Hijrah, in Makkah.
After ‘Eesā’s return mankind will accept other religions.
Mankind will accept ONLY Islam.
Test Yourselfcover the right column
1. Write the Prophet’s ﷺ full five-name lineage.Muhammad ibn ‘Abdillah ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hāshim ibn ‘Abd Manāf ﷺ.
2. What is the proof that he is the Seal of the Prophets?Al-Aḥzāb 33:40.
3. At what age did revelation begin? How long was his mission in total?40 · 23 years (13 Makkah + 10 Madinah).
4. How many years did he call in secret?3.
5. At what age did he pass away?63.
6. What became obligatory during the Isrā’ and Mi‘rāj?The five daily prayers.
7. Who was the first messenger? Who is last in time but first in rank?Nūḥ · Muhammad ﷺ.
8. Put in order: Hijrah, revelation at 40, death at 63, Isrā’ & Mi‘rāj, 13 years in Makkah.Revelation at 40 → 13 years in Makkah → Isrā’ & Mi‘rāj → Hijrah → death at 63.

Tawhid Study Guide 10
The Poem — Lines & Sections
SG 10
Hides every gold word and answer so you can quiz yourself — click any hidden box to reveal it.
Assessed in:CW 14CW 15HW 14HW 15QZ 10TS 10EX 4
The poem is the same book in verse (naẓm), written so it can be memorized more easily. It has 13 named sections, opening with مُقَدِّمَة (the Introduction) and closing with نُزُولُ عِيسَى وَالْخَاتِمَة. Every line the assessments ask you to complete is below, in order — the gold word is the one you must supply.
Sections the Assessments Name
Section
Meaning
مُقَدِّمَة
Introduction
مَعْرِفَةُ رَبِّكَ
Knowing your Lord
قُبْحُ الشِّرْك
The Ugliness of Shirk
أَوَّلُ مَا فَرَضَ اللَّهُ
The first thing Allah made obligatory
الْإِيمَانُ بِالْبَعْث
Belief in the Resurrection
مَعْرِفَةُ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ
Knowing the Prophet ﷺ
عُمْرُهُ الْمُبَارَك وَالْإِسْرَاء وَالْمِعْرَاج
His blessed life, and the Night Journey
أَوَّلُ الرُّسُلِ وَآخِرُهُمْ وَأَفْضَلُهُم
First, Last & Best of the Messengers
نُزُولُ عِيسَى وَالْخَاتِمَة
‘Eesa’s Descent & the Closing
Lines to Memorize (1 of 2)gold word = what the assessments ask you to supply
وَبَعْدُ فَاعْلَمْ أَنَّمَا التَّوْحِيدُ لَا شَيْءَ قَطُّ دُونَهُ يُفِيدُKnow that Tawhid comes first — nothing at all benefits a person without it.
إِنْ قِيلَ مَنْ رَبُّكَ قُلْتَ اللَّهُIf asked “Who is your Lord?”, say: Allah.
وَذُو الْأُلُوهِيَّةِ قُلْ مَعْنَاهُ تَعْرِفُهُ بِالْخَلْقِ يَا ذَا اللُّبِّ
كَالْأَرْضِ وَالسَّمَاءِ وَالْآيَاتِ كَالشَّمْسِ وَالْبَدْرِ وَكَالسَّاعَاتِSigns: the earth, the sky, the sun, the moon, the passing hours.
وَغَايَةُ الْخَلْقِ هِيَ الْعِبَادَةْ لِلَّهِ وَحْدَهُ كَمَا الشَّهَادَةْThe purpose of creation is worship — of Allah alone, just as the testimony of faith declares.

Tawhid Study Guide 10 · The Poem — Lines & Sections — page 2 of 4
Lines to Memorize (2 of 2)
وَذَاكَ بِامْتِثَالِكَ الْأَوَامِرَا كَذَلِكَ اجْتِنَابُكَ الزَّوَاجِرَا
بِشَرْطِ إِخْلَاصٍ بِلَا رِيَاءِ مَعَ اتِّبَاعِ خَيْرِ الْأَنْبِيَاءِWorship needs sincerity without showing off, and following the best of the prophets ﷺ.
وَالشِّرْكُ أَقْبَحُ الذُّنُوبِ فَاجْتَنِبْ صَرْفُ عِبَادَةٍ لِمَخْلُوقٍ تُصِبْShirk is the ugliest of sins — avoid directing worship to a created being.
مَنْ يَدْعُ غَيْرَ اللَّهِ مَدْعُوهُ عَبَدْ لَا تَدْعُ غَيْرَ اللَّهِ فَاللَّهُ الصَّمَدْWhoever calls upon other than Allah has worshipped what he called upon — do not call upon other than Allah, for Allah is As-Samad.
وَالْكُفْرُ بِالطَّاغُوتِ فَرْضٌ أَوَّلَا لِلْمُؤْمِنِ بِاللَّهِ جَلَّ وَعَلَاRejecting Taghut is the first obligation on the one who believes in Allah.
وَكُلُّ مَا جَاوَزَ عَبْدٌ حَدَّهُ حَتَّى الْمُطَاعُ فَالطَّاغُوتُ حُدَّهُ
وَدِينُكَ الْإِسْلَامُ الِاسْتِسْلَامُ لِلَّهِ بِالتَّوْحِيدِ وَالْقِيَامُ
بِالْخَمْسَةِ الْأَرْكَانِ كَالصَّلَاةِ وَالصَّوْمِ وَالْحَجِّ مَعَ الزَّكَاةِThe five pillars: prayer, fasting, Hajj, with Zakah (and the testimonies).
وَذَاكَ دِينُ اللَّهِ لِلْعِبَادِ مِنْ خَلْقِ آدَمَ وَلِلْمَعَادِ
وَالسِّتَّةُ الْأَرْكَانُ لِلْإِيمَانِ إِيمَانُنَا بِاللَّهِ ذِي الْإِحْسَانِ
وَالرُّسُلِ وَالسَّاعَةِ وَالَّذِي كُتِبْ وَبِالْمَلَائِكِ الْكِرَامِ وَالْكُتُبْ“وَالَّذِي كُتِبْ” = Al-Qadar (what has been written/decreed).
وَجَاحِدُ الْبَعْثِ فَفِي النِّيرَانِ مُخَلَّدًا حَقًّا لِذِي الْكُفْرَانِWhoever denies the resurrection is in the Fire forever — truly, for the disbeliever.
وَقُلْ خِتَامُ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ مُحَمَّدُ لِلْعَالَمِينَ مُرْسَلٌ كَيْ يَهْتَدُوا
وَأَرْبَعُونَ عُمْرُهُ فِي الْبَعْثَةِ وَبَعْدَ عِشْرِينَ ثَلَاثُ الدَّعْوَةِForty was his age at the start of the mission; then twenty-three years of calling.

Watch Out — Common Mistakes
The poem was written to be harder to memorize than the prose book.
It was written to make memorization EASIER.
نُزُولُ عِيسَى وَالْخَاتِمَة is the poem’s first section.
It is the poem’s LAST (closing) section; the first is مُقَدِّمَة.

Read each guide once, then use Cover answers on this sheet to test yourself.
SG 1 · Lesson 0 · Introductionmust-know facts
  • The unit is based on the book Ta’līm aṣ-Ṣibyān at-Tawḥīd by Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab. The poem (naẓm) is the same book in verse.
  • The poem exists so the content can be memorized more easily.
  • Every answer in the book is given with a dalīl (Qur’an or ḥadīth proof).
  • Al-Fiṭrah is natural — it is not a belief taught from scratch.
  • The goal is understanding — not repeating answers without knowing the dalīl behind them.
SG 2 · Lesson 1 · Q1–Q2 — Who is your Lord?must-know facts
  • Ar-Rabb has six meanings — Creator, Owner, Provider, Helper, Supporter, and the One Worshipped. It does not have just one.
  • Rabb points to Allah’s lordship and His actions. Allah points to His unique right to be worshipped. They are not exact synonyms.
  • Al-Ulūhiyyah is the quality of deserving worship — not merely creating.
  • One proof — Al-A‘rāf 7:54 — answers Q1, Q2 and Q3 together.
  • الشَّهِيد (Witness) is not one of the six meanings.
AMAN · amanschoolmn.orgYouth Educated… Family Cultivated… World IlluminatedT1 Guide · p1/4
Test 1 Study Guide · Lessons 0-2 · Intro, Rabb & His Signs — page 2 of 4
SG 3 · Lesson 2 · Q3 — His Signsmust-know facts
  • A sign is what Allah alone does — the sun, moon, earth, sky. Man-made things (a drawing, video game, toy, cartoon) are not signs of Allah.
  • The poem lists five signs: the earth, the sky, the sun, the moon, and the passing hours. Night and day changing is also a sign.
  • Signs are found in creation itself — not only in the Qur’an’s text. The Qur’an describes creation as a proof pointing to the Creator.
  • We do not know Allah only because someone told us — His signs show Him too.
  • Why it matters: it should lead to gratitude, remembrance (dhikr) and worship — not taking creation for granted.

SG 4 · IbadahSG 5 · Shirk
Read each guide once, then use Cover answers on this sheet to test yourself.
SG 4 · Lesson 3 · Q4 — Purpose & Ibadahmust-know facts
  • The purpose of creation is worship of Allah alone.
  • Q4 has two proofs: Adh-Dhāriyāt 51:56 and An-Nisā’ 4:36. (Al-Ikhlāṣ 112:1 is not one of them.)
  • Ibādah is a comprehensive term for everything Allah loves and is pleased with — far more than the five prayers. This definition is credited to Ibn Taymiyyah.
  • Two conditions for accepted worship — Ikhlāṣ and Mutāba‘ah. A deed needs both together; looking correct outwardly is not enough.
  • Riyā’ ruins sincerity — the deed is no longer purely for Allah, so it can be rejected.
SG 5 · Lesson 4 · Shirk — Definitions & Proofsmust-know facts
  • Shirk = making a nidd for Allah — calling on it, hoping in it, fearing it, relying on it, or having strong desire toward it, besides Allah.
  • Five types of worship where Shirk can occur: Du‘ā, Khawf, Rajā’, Tawakkul, Mahabbah. (Ṣalāh is not on this list.)
  • Khawf becomes Shirk if directed to other than Allah in a controlling way. Rajā’: hoping in a creation the way one hopes in Allah. Tawakkul: relying totally on other than Allah.
  • Full trust in Allah while using permitted means (like studying for a test) is correct Tawakkul — not Shirk.
  • Shirk is the greatest of all sins — not a minor or easily forgivable one.

SG 6 · TaghutSG 7 · Islam
Read each guide once, then use Cover answers on this sheet to test yourself.
SG 6 · Lesson 5 · Taghut — Definition & the First Obligationmust-know facts
  • The definition of Ṭāghūt taught in class is credited to Ibn al-Qayyim. Three categories: something worshipped, followed, or obeyed besides Allah.
  • First obligation on every servant: kufr bi-Ṭāghūt and īmān billāh. Rejecting Ṭāghūt is obligatory for every believer — never optional.
  • An-Naḥl 16:36: every messenger to every nation called: worship Allah and avoid Ṭāghūt.
  • Lā ilāha illa Allāh negates everything false FIRST (لَا إِلَهَ), then affirms Allah (إِلَّا اللَّه) — the same order as kufr bi-Ṭāghūt before īmān billāh.
  • Examples: a Kāhin, a Munajjim, someone obeyed while commanding disobedience to Allah. Modern: horoscopes/fortune-telling, a person or ideology obeyed even in sin, wealth or fame treated as life’s ultimate purpose.
  • Consulting a fortune-teller “just to check” is forbidden and undermines correct worship. A person cannot be a complete believer while following a Ṭāghūt.
AMAN · amanschoolmn.orgYouth Educated… Family Cultivated… World IlluminatedT3 Guide · p1/4
Test 3 Study Guide · Lessons 5-6 · Taghut & Islam — page 2 of 4
SG 7 · Lesson 6 · Q5 — Islam & the Five Pillarsmust-know facts
  • Four components of Islam: (1) submission through Tawḥīd, (2) compliance through obedience, (3) allegiance toward Muslims, (4) rejection of Shirk and its people.
  • Why belief alone is not enough: Islam also requires actual obedience, loyalty to fellow believers, and active rejection of Shirk.
  • Five pillars: Shahādatayn, Ṣalāh, Zakah, Ṣawm, Ḥajj. Zakah is a pillar. Jihad is not one of the five.
  • Hajj is obligatory only on those who are able (physically and financially).
  • Islam is the religion of Allah for ALL His servants — not only Arabs — from the creation of Ādam on.

SG 8 · Lesson 6 · Īmān & the Unseenmust-know facts
  • The six pillars of Īmān: Allah, the Angels, the Books, the Messengers, the Last Day, and Al-Qadar.
  • All six must be believed in together — a person cannot pick and choose. The Five Pillars of Islam are not one of the six.
  • A believer must accept Al-Qadar in both the good and the difficult decree. In the poem, وَالَّذِي كُتِبْ refers to Al-Qadar.
  • Al-Ba‘th is coming back to life after death. Denying it is Kufr — it is one of the six pillars, a foundation, not optional.
  • After being raised, people face Jannah, the Fire, and al-Ḥisāb.

SG 9 · Prophet ﷺ
Read each guide once, then use Cover answers on this sheet to test yourself.
SG 9 · Lesson 7 · Q6 — The Prophet ﷺmust-know facts
  • Lineage: Muhammad ibn ‘Abdillah ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hāshim ibn ‘Abd Manāf ﷺ. Proof that he is the Seal: Al-Aḥzāb 33:40.
  • He ﷺ was sent to ALL of humanity (الأَحْمَر وَالأَسْوَد), not only the Arabs. There is no prophet after him.
  • Revelation began at 40. He called for 23 years total: 13 in Makkah (3 in secret) and 10 in Madinah. He passed away at 63, after the religion was completed and perfected.
  • The Isrā’ and Mi‘rāj happened before the Hijrah, still in Makkah — the five daily prayers were made obligatory then.
  • Nūḥ was the first messenger (after Shirk appeared). Muhammad ﷺ is the last in time but first in rank.
  • The four rightly-guided caliphs, in order: Abū Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Uthmān, ‘Alī.
  • Best generations: the Ṣaḥābah, then the Tābi‘ūn, then the Followers of the Followers.
  • ‘Eesā will descend near the end of time, break the cross, the swine will be killed — and mankind will accept ONLY Islam.

Study Path — in this orderclick to open
SG 1 · IntroSG 2 · RabbSG 3 · SignsSG 4 · IbadahSG 5 · Shirk
Read each guide once, then use Cover answers on this sheet to test yourself.
SG 1 · Lesson 0 · Introductionmust-know facts
  • The unit is based on the book Ta’līm aṣ-Ṣibyān at-Tawḥīd by Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab. The poem (naẓm) is the same book in verse.
  • The poem exists so the content can be memorized more easily.
  • Every answer in the book is given with a dalīl (Qur’an or ḥadīth proof).
  • Al-Fiṭrah is natural — it is not a belief taught from scratch.
  • The goal is understanding — not repeating answers without knowing the dalīl behind them.
SG 2 · Lesson 1 · Q1–Q2 — Who is your Lord?must-know facts
  • Ar-Rabb has six meanings — Creator, Owner, Provider, Helper, Supporter, and the One Worshipped. It does not have just one.
  • Rabb points to Allah’s lordship and His actions. Allah points to His unique right to be worshipped. They are not exact synonyms.
  • Al-Ulūhiyyah is the quality of deserving worship — not merely creating.
  • One proof — Al-A‘rāf 7:54 — answers Q1, Q2 and Q3 together.
  • الشَّهِيد (Witness) is not one of the six meanings.
AMAN · amanschoolmn.orgYouth Educated… Family Cultivated… World IlluminatedT6 Guide · p1/5
Test 6 Study Guide · Cumulative A · Lessons 0-4 — page 2 of 5
SG 3 · Lesson 2 · Q3 — His Signsmust-know facts
  • A sign is what Allah alone does — the sun, moon, earth, sky. Man-made things (a drawing, video game, toy, cartoon) are not signs of Allah.
  • The poem lists five signs: the earth, the sky, the sun, the moon, and the passing hours. Night and day changing is also a sign.
  • Signs are found in creation itself — not only in the Qur’an’s text. The Qur’an describes creation as a proof pointing to the Creator.
  • We do not know Allah only because someone told us — His signs show Him too.
  • Why it matters: it should lead to gratitude, remembrance (dhikr) and worship — not taking creation for granted.
SG 4 · Lesson 3 · Q4 — Purpose & Ibadahmust-know facts
  • The purpose of creation is worship of Allah alone.
  • Q4 has two proofs: Adh-Dhāriyāt 51:56 and An-Nisā’ 4:36. (Al-Ikhlāṣ 112:1 is not one of them.)
  • Ibādah is a comprehensive term for everything Allah loves and is pleased with — far more than the five prayers. This definition is credited to Ibn Taymiyyah.
  • Two conditions for accepted worship — Ikhlāṣ and Mutāba‘ah. A deed needs both together; looking correct outwardly is not enough.
  • Riyā’ ruins sincerity — the deed is no longer purely for Allah, so it can be rejected.
SG 5 · Lesson 4 · Shirk — Definitions & Proofsmust-know facts
  • Shirk = making a nidd for Allah — calling on it, hoping in it, fearing it, relying on it, or having strong desire toward it, besides Allah.
  • Five types of worship where Shirk can occur: Du‘ā, Khawf, Rajā’, Tawakkul, Mahabbah. (Ṣalāh is not on this list.)
  • Khawf becomes Shirk if directed to other than Allah in a controlling way. Rajā’: hoping in a creation the way one hopes in Allah. Tawakkul: relying totally on other than Allah.
  • Full trust in Allah while using permitted means (like studying for a test) is correct Tawakkul — not Shirk.
  • Shirk is the greatest of all sins — not a minor or easily forgivable one.
AMAN · amanschoolmn.orgYouth Educated… Family Cultivated… World IlluminatedT6 Guide · p2/5

Du‘ā IS an act of worship.
Az-Zumar 39:64-66
Shirk nullifies ALL good deeds — even hypothetically warning the Prophet ﷺ.

Al-Fiṭrah is the natural disposition every person is born with.

Every answer is given with a dalīl.

SG 6 · TaghutSG 7 · IslamSG 8 · ImanSG 9 · Prophet ﷺ
Read each guide once, then use Cover answers on this sheet to test yourself.
SG 6 · Lesson 5 · Taghut — Definition & the First Obligationmust-know facts
  • The definition of Ṭāghūt taught in class is credited to Ibn al-Qayyim. Three categories: something worshipped, followed, or obeyed besides Allah.
  • First obligation on every servant: kufr bi-Ṭāghūt and īmān billāh. Rejecting Ṭāghūt is obligatory for every believer — never optional.
  • An-Naḥl 16:36: every messenger to every nation called: worship Allah and avoid Ṭāghūt.
  • Lā ilāha illa Allāh negates everything false FIRST (لَا إِلَهَ), then affirms Allah (إِلَّا اللَّه) — the same order as kufr bi-Ṭāghūt before īmān billāh.
  • Examples: a Kāhin, a Munajjim, someone obeyed while commanding disobedience to Allah. Modern: horoscopes/fortune-telling, a person or ideology obeyed even in sin, wealth or fame treated as life’s ultimate purpose.
  • Consulting a fortune-teller “just to check” is forbidden and undermines correct worship. A person cannot be a complete believer while following a Ṭāghūt.
SG 7 · Lesson 6 · Q5 — Islam & the Five Pillarsmust-know facts
  • Four components of Islam: (1) submission through Tawḥīd, (2) compliance through obedience, (3) allegiance toward Muslims, (4) rejection of Shirk and its people.
  • Why belief alone is not enough: Islam also requires actual obedience, loyalty to fellow believers, and active rejection of Shirk.
  • Five pillars: Shahādatayn, Ṣalāh, Zakah, Ṣawm, Ḥajj. Zakah is a pillar. Jihad is not one of the five.
  • Hajj is obligatory only on those who are able (physically and financially).
  • Islam is the religion of Allah for ALL His servants — not only Arabs — from the creation of Ādam on.
AMAN · amanschoolmn.orgYouth Educated… Family Cultivated… World IlluminatedT7 Guide · p1/4
Test 7 Study Guide · Cumulative B · Lessons 5-8 — page 2 of 4
SG 8 · Lesson 6 · Īmān & the Unseenmust-know facts
  • The six pillars of Īmān: Allah, the Angels, the Books, the Messengers, the Last Day, and Al-Qadar.
  • All six must be believed in together — a person cannot pick and choose. The Five Pillars of Islam are not one of the six.
  • A believer must accept Al-Qadar in both the good and the difficult decree. In the poem, وَالَّذِي كُتِبْ refers to Al-Qadar.
  • Al-Ba‘th is coming back to life after death. Denying it is Kufr — it is one of the six pillars, a foundation, not optional.
  • After being raised, people face Jannah, the Fire, and al-Ḥisāb.
SG 9 · Lesson 7 · Q6 — The Prophet ﷺmust-know facts
  • Lineage: Muhammad ibn ‘Abdillah ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hāshim ibn ‘Abd Manāf ﷺ. Proof that he is the Seal: Al-Aḥzāb 33:40.
  • He ﷺ was sent to ALL of humanity (الأَحْمَر وَالأَسْوَد), not only the Arabs. There is no prophet after him.
  • Revelation began at 40. He called for 23 years total: 13 in Makkah (3 in secret) and 10 in Madinah. He passed away at 63, after the religion was completed and perfected.
  • The Isrā’ and Mi‘rāj happened before the Hijrah, still in Makkah — the five daily prayers were made obligatory then.
  • Nūḥ was the first messenger (after Shirk appeared). Muhammad ﷺ is the last in time but first in rank.
  • The four rightly-guided caliphs, in order: Abū Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Uthmān, ‘Alī.
  • Best generations: the Ṣaḥābah, then the Tābi‘ūn, then the Followers of the Followers.
  • ‘Eesā will descend near the end of time, break the cross, the swine will be killed — and mankind will accept ONLY Islam.
Proofs (Dalīl) you may be asked for
An-Naḥl 16:36
Every messenger to every nation: worship Allah and avoid Taghut.
Āl-‘Imrān 3:19
The religion accepted by Allah is Islam.
Āl-‘Imrān 3:85
Seeking a religion other than Islam is never accepted.
Al-Bayyinah 98:5
Proof for the first three pillars (Shahādatayn, Ṣalāh, Zakah).
Al-Baqarah 2:183
Proof that fasting is obligatory.
Āl-‘Imrān 3:97
Proof for Hajj — on those who are able.
Ar-Ra‘d 13:5
Calls denial of the resurrection an astonishing statement.

Watch Out — Common Mistakes
The first obligation is belief in Allah, before disbelief in Ṭāghūt.
Kufr bi-Ṭāghūt comes first (then īmān billāh).
A person can be a complete believer while following a Ṭāghūt.
He cannot.
Rejecting Ṭāghūt is optional for a “strong enough” believer.
It is obligatory for every believer.
You can worship Allah correctly and still visit a fortune-teller “just to check.”
That is forbidden and undermines correct worship.
Islam has only two components.
Islam has FOUR components.
Zakah is not one of the five pillars.
Zakah IS a pillar.
Common Mistakes (continued)
Hajj is obligatory on every Muslim regardless of ability.
Hajj is only for those who are able.
Islam is only for Arabs.
Islam is Allah’s religion for ALL His servants.
Al-Qadar only needs to be believed in when the decree is good.
Both the good and the difficult decree.
A person can pick and choose which pillars to believe in.
All six must be believed in together.
The Five Pillars of Islam are one of the six pillars of Īmān.
They are not — the six are Allah, Angels, Books, Messengers, Last Day, Al-Qadar.
Khātam an-Nabiyyīn means the first of the prophets.
It means the Seal (last) of the prophets.
Common Mistakes (continued)
The Prophet ﷺ was sent only to the Arabs.
He ﷺ was sent to all of humanity.
The Isrā’ and Mi‘rāj happened after the Hijrah.
They happened before the Hijrah, in Makkah.
After ‘Eesā’s return mankind will accept other religions.
Mankind will accept ONLY Islam.

Watch Out — Common Mistakes

It was written to make memorization EASIER.

SG 1 · IntroSG 2 · RabbSG 3 · SignsSG 4 · IbadahSG 5 · Shirk
Read each guide once, then use Cover answers on this sheet to test yourself.
SG 1 · Lesson 0 · Introductionmust-know facts
  • The unit is based on the book Ta’līm aṣ-Ṣibyān at-Tawḥīd by Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab. The poem (naẓm) is the same book in verse.
  • The poem exists so the content can be memorized more easily.
  • Every answer in the book is given with a dalīl (Qur’an or ḥadīth proof).
  • Al-Fiṭrah is natural — it is not a belief taught from scratch.
  • The goal is understanding — not repeating answers without knowing the dalīl behind them.
SG 2 · Lesson 1 · Q1–Q2 — Who is your Lord?must-know facts
  • Ar-Rabb has six meanings — Creator, Owner, Provider, Helper, Supporter, and the One Worshipped. It does not have just one.
  • Rabb points to Allah’s lordship and His actions. Allah points to His unique right to be worshipped. They are not exact synonyms.
  • Al-Ulūhiyyah is the quality of deserving worship — not merely creating.
  • One proof — Al-A‘rāf 7:54 — answers Q1, Q2 and Q3 together.
  • الشَّهِيد (Witness) is not one of the six meanings.
AMAN · amanschoolmn.orgYouth Educated… Family Cultivated… World IlluminatedE1 Guide · p1/5
Exam 1 Study Guide · Midterm · Lessons 0-4 — page 2 of 5
SG 3 · Lesson 2 · Q3 — His Signsmust-know facts
  • A sign is what Allah alone does — the sun, moon, earth, sky. Man-made things (a drawing, video game, toy, cartoon) are not signs of Allah.
  • The poem lists five signs: the earth, the sky, the sun, the moon, and the passing hours. Night and day changing is also a sign.
  • Signs are found in creation itself — not only in the Qur’an’s text. The Qur’an describes creation as a proof pointing to the Creator.
  • We do not know Allah only because someone told us — His signs show Him too.
  • Why it matters: it should lead to gratitude, remembrance (dhikr) and worship — not taking creation for granted.
SG 4 · Lesson 3 · Q4 — Purpose & Ibadahmust-know facts
  • The purpose of creation is worship of Allah alone.
  • Q4 has two proofs: Adh-Dhāriyāt 51:56 and An-Nisā’ 4:36. (Al-Ikhlāṣ 112:1 is not one of them.)
  • Ibādah is a comprehensive term for everything Allah loves and is pleased with — far more than the five prayers. This definition is credited to Ibn Taymiyyah.
  • Two conditions for accepted worship — Ikhlāṣ and Mutāba‘ah. A deed needs both together; looking correct outwardly is not enough.
  • Riyā’ ruins sincerity — the deed is no longer purely for Allah, so it can be rejected.
SG 5 · Lesson 4 · Shirk — Definitions & Proofsmust-know facts
  • Shirk = making a nidd for Allah — calling on it, hoping in it, fearing it, relying on it, or having strong desire toward it, besides Allah.
  • Five types of worship where Shirk can occur: Du‘ā, Khawf, Rajā’, Tawakkul, Mahabbah. (Ṣalāh is not on this list.)
  • Khawf becomes Shirk if directed to other than Allah in a controlling way. Rajā’: hoping in a creation the way one hopes in Allah. Tawakkul: relying totally on other than Allah.
  • Full trust in Allah while using permitted means (like studying for a test) is correct Tawakkul — not Shirk.
  • Shirk is the greatest of all sins — not a minor or easily forgivable one.
AMAN · amanschoolmn.orgYouth Educated… Family Cultivated… World IlluminatedE1 Guide · p2/5
Exam 1 Study Guide · Midterm · Lessons 0-4 — page 3 of 5
Proofs (Dalīl) you may be asked for
Al-A‘rāf 7:54
Answers Q1, Q2 and Q3 together — heavens and earth created in six days.
Adh-Dhāriyāt 51:56
“I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Me.”
An-Nisā’ 4:36
Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him.
Al-Mā’idah 5:72
Shirk forbids Jannah; one’s home becomes the Fire.
Al-Jinn 72:18
Mosques are for Allah — do not call on anyone besides Him.
Al-Mu’minūn 23:117
Du‘ā to another deity = Kufr. Such a person will NOT succeed (لَا يُفْلِحُ الْكَافِرُونَ).
Ghāfir 40:60
Du‘ā IS an act of worship.
Az-Zumar 39:64-66
Shirk nullifies ALL good deeds — even hypothetically warning the Prophet ﷺ.
Watch Out — Common Mistakes
The book was written by Ibn al-Qayyim.
Written by Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab.
Sibyān means adult scholars.
Sibyān means children / young boys.
Deeds still benefit a person without Tawḥīd.
Nothing at all benefits a person without Tawḥīd.
Al-Fiṭrah is something taught from scratch.
Al-Fiṭrah is the natural disposition every person is born with.
Some answers in the book come with no proof.
Every answer is given with a dalīl.
Ar-Rabb has only one meaning: Creator.
Ar-Rabb has six meanings.

Exam 1 Study Guide · Midterm · Lessons 0-4 — page 4 of 5
Common Mistakes (continued)
Rabb and Allāh mean exactly the same thing.
Rabb points to lordship/actions; Allāh to the unique right to be worshipped.
The proof for Q1–Q3 is from Al-Baqarah.
The proof is Al-A‘rāf 7:54.
Al-Ulūhiyyah means being a creator only.
Al-Ulūhiyyah means truly deserving worship.
“Witness” is one of the six meanings of Rabb.
The six are Creator, Owner, Provider, Helper, Supporter, One Worshipped.
A drawing or video game counts as a sign of Allah.
Man-made things are not signs — signs are what Allah alone does.
Signs can only be found in the Qur’an.
Signs are in creation itself, not only the Qur’an’s text.
Common Mistakes (continued)
We know Allah only because someone told us.
We also know Him through His signs and creation.
Ibādah is only the five daily prayers.
Ibādah is everything Allah loves and is pleased with.
The proof for Q4 is only one ayah.
Q4 has two proofs: Adh-Dhāriyāt 51:56 and An-Nisā’ 4:36.
A deed is accepted even without sincerity if it looks correct.
A deed needs sincerity AND following the Prophet ﷺ.
Riyā’ strengthens sincerity.
Riyā’ ruins sincerity.
One of the two conditions is enough.
Both conditions are needed together.
Common Mistakes (continued)
Shirk is a minor, easily forgivable sin.
Shirk is the greatest of all sins.
Al-Mu’minūn 23:117 says calling on another deity leads to success.
Such a person will NOT succeed.
Khawf can never become Shirk.
Khawf CAN become Shirk if directed to other than Allah in a controlling way.
Trusting Allah while studying for a test is Shirk.
Using permitted means with trust in Allah is correct Tawakkul.

Exam 2 Study Guide · Final · Lessons 0-8 — page 3 of 8
SG 6 · Lesson 5 · Taghut — Definition & the First Obligationmust-know facts
  • The definition of Ṭāghūt taught in class is credited to Ibn al-Qayyim. Three categories: something worshipped, followed, or obeyed besides Allah.
  • First obligation on every servant: kufr bi-Ṭāghūt and īmān billāh. Rejecting Ṭāghūt is obligatory for every believer — never optional.
  • An-Naḥl 16:36: every messenger to every nation called: worship Allah and avoid Ṭāghūt.
  • Lā ilāha illa Allāh negates everything false FIRST (لَا إِلَهَ), then affirms Allah (إِلَّا اللَّه) — the same order as kufr bi-Ṭāghūt before īmān billāh.
  • Examples: a Kāhin, a Munajjim, someone obeyed while commanding disobedience to Allah. Modern: horoscopes/fortune-telling, a person or ideology obeyed even in sin, wealth or fame treated as life’s ultimate purpose.
  • Consulting a fortune-teller “just to check” is forbidden and undermines correct worship. A person cannot be a complete believer while following a Ṭāghūt.
SG 7 · Lesson 6 · Q5 — Islam & the Five Pillarsmust-know facts
  • Four components of Islam: (1) submission through Tawḥīd, (2) compliance through obedience, (3) allegiance toward Muslims, (4) rejection of Shirk and its people.
  • Why belief alone is not enough: Islam also requires actual obedience, loyalty to fellow believers, and active rejection of Shirk.
  • Five pillars: Shahādatayn, Ṣalāh, Zakah, Ṣawm, Ḥajj. Zakah is a pillar. Jihad is not one of the five.
  • Hajj is obligatory only on those who are able (physically and financially).
  • Islam is the religion of Allah for ALL His servants — not only Arabs — from the creation of Ādam on.
SG 8 · Lesson 6 · Īmān & the Unseenmust-know facts
  • The six pillars of Īmān: Allah, the Angels, the Books, the Messengers, the Last Day, and Al-Qadar.
  • All six must be believed in together — a person cannot pick and choose. The Five Pillars of Islam are not one of the six.
  • A believer must accept Al-Qadar in both the good and the difficult decree. In the poem, وَالَّذِي كُتِبْ refers to Al-Qadar.
  • Al-Ba‘th is coming back to life after death. Denying it is Kufr — it is one of the six pillars, a foundation, not optional.
  • After being raised, people face Jannah, the Fire, and al-Ḥisāb.
AMAN · amanschoolmn.orgYouth Educated… Family Cultivated… World IlluminatedE2 Guide · p3/8
Exam 2 Study Guide · Final · Lessons 0-8 — page 4 of 8
SG 9 · Lesson 7 · Q6 — The Prophet ﷺmust-know facts
  • Lineage: Muhammad ibn ‘Abdillah ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hāshim ibn ‘Abd Manāf ﷺ. Proof that he is the Seal: Al-Aḥzāb 33:40.
  • He ﷺ was sent to ALL of humanity (الأَحْمَر وَالأَسْوَد), not only the Arabs. There is no prophet after him.
  • Revelation began at 40. He called for 23 years total: 13 in Makkah (3 in secret) and 10 in Madinah. He passed away at 63, after the religion was completed and perfected.
  • The Isrā’ and Mi‘rāj happened before the Hijrah, still in Makkah — the five daily prayers were made obligatory then.
  • Nūḥ was the first messenger (after Shirk appeared). Muhammad ﷺ is the last in time but first in rank.
  • The four rightly-guided caliphs, in order: Abū Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Uthmān, ‘Alī.
  • Best generations: the Ṣaḥābah, then the Tābi‘ūn, then the Followers of the Followers.
  • ‘Eesā will descend near the end of time, break the cross, the swine will be killed — and mankind will accept ONLY Islam.
Proofs (Dalīl) you may be asked for
Al-A‘rāf 7:54
Answers Q1, Q2 and Q3 together — heavens and earth created in six days.
Adh-Dhāriyāt 51:56
“I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Me.”
An-Nisā’ 4:36
Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him.
Al-Mā’idah 5:72
Shirk forbids Jannah; one’s home becomes the Fire.
Al-Jinn 72:18
Mosques are for Allah — do not call on anyone besides Him.
Al-Mu’minūn 23:117
Du‘ā to another deity = Kufr. Such a person will NOT succeed (لَا يُفْلِحُ الْكَافِرُونَ).
Ghāfir 40:60
Du‘ā IS an act of worship.
Az-Zumar 39:64-66
Shirk nullifies ALL good deeds — even hypothetically warning the Prophet ﷺ.

Āl-‘Imrān 3:19

Āl-‘Imrān 3:85

Watch Out — Common Mistakes
The book was written by Ibn al-Qayyim.
Written by Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab.
Sibyān means adult scholars.
Sibyān means children / young boys.
Deeds still benefit a person without Tawḥīd.
Nothing at all benefits a person without Tawḥīd.
Al-Fiṭrah is something taught from scratch.
Al-Fiṭrah is the natural disposition every person is born with.
Some answers in the book come with no proof.
Every answer is given with a dalīl.
Ar-Rabb has only one meaning: Creator.
Ar-Rabb has six meanings.
Common Mistakes (continued)
Rabb and Allāh mean exactly the same thing.
Rabb points to lordship/actions; Allāh to the unique right to be worshipped.
The proof for Q1–Q3 is from Al-Baqarah.
The proof is Al-A‘rāf 7:54.
Al-Ulūhiyyah means being a creator only.
Al-Ulūhiyyah means truly deserving worship.
“Witness” is one of the six meanings of Rabb.
The six are Creator, Owner, Provider, Helper, Supporter, One Worshipped.
A drawing or video game counts as a sign of Allah.
Man-made things are not signs — signs are what Allah alone does.
Signs can only be found in the Qur’an.
Signs are in creation itself, not only the Qur’an’s text.
AMAN · amanschoolmn.orgYouth Educated… Family Cultivated… World IlluminatedE2 Guide · p5/8
Exam 2 Study Guide · Final · Lessons 0-8 — page 6 of 8
Common Mistakes (continued)
We know Allah only because someone told us.
We also know Him through His signs and creation.
Ibādah is only the five daily prayers.
Ibādah is everything Allah loves and is pleased with.
The proof for Q4 is only one ayah.
Q4 has two proofs: Adh-Dhāriyāt 51:56 and An-Nisā’ 4:36.
A deed is accepted even without sincerity if it looks correct.
A deed needs sincerity AND following the Prophet ﷺ.
Riyā’ strengthens sincerity.
Riyā’ ruins sincerity.
One of the two conditions is enough.
Both conditions are needed together.
Common Mistakes (continued)
Shirk is a minor, easily forgivable sin.
Shirk is the greatest of all sins.
Al-Mu’minūn 23:117 says calling on another deity leads to success.
Such a person will NOT succeed.
Khawf can never become Shirk.
Khawf CAN become Shirk if directed to other than Allah in a controlling way.
Trusting Allah while studying for a test is Shirk.
Using permitted means with trust in Allah is correct Tawakkul.
The first obligation is belief in Allah, before disbelief in Ṭāghūt.
Kufr bi-Ṭāghūt comes first (then īmān billāh).
A person can be a complete believer while following a Ṭāghūt.
He cannot.
Common Mistakes (continued)
Rejecting Ṭāghūt is optional for a “strong enough” believer.
It is obligatory for every believer.
You can worship Allah correctly and still visit a fortune-teller “just to check.”
That is forbidden and undermines correct worship.
Islam has only two components.
Islam has FOUR components.
Zakah is not one of the five pillars.
Zakah IS a pillar.
Hajj is obligatory on every Muslim regardless of ability.
Hajj is only for those who are able.
Islam is only for Arabs.
Islam is Allah’s religion for ALL His servants.
AMAN · amanschoolmn.orgYouth Educated… Family Cultivated… World IlluminatedE2 Guide · p6/8
Exam 2 Study Guide · Final · Lessons 0-8 — page 7 of 8
Common Mistakes (continued)
Al-Qadar only needs to be believed in when the decree is good.
Both the good and the difficult decree.
A person can pick and choose which pillars to believe in.
All six must be believed in together.
The Five Pillars of Islam are one of the six pillars of Īmān.
They are not — the six are Allah, Angels, Books, Messengers, Last Day, Al-Qadar.
Khātam an-Nabiyyīn means the first of the prophets.
It means the Seal (last) of the prophets.
The Prophet ﷺ was sent only to the Arabs.
He ﷺ was sent to all of humanity.
The Isrā’ and Mi‘rāj happened after the Hijrah.
They happened before the Hijrah, in Makkah.
Common Mistakes (continued)
After ‘Eesā’s return mankind will accept other religions.
Mankind will accept ONLY Islam.

Watch Out — Common Mistakes
The poem was written to be harder to memorize than the prose book.
It was written to make memorization EASIER.
نُزُولُ عِيسَى وَالْخَاتِمَة is the poem’s first section.
It is the poem’s LAST (closing) section; the first is مُقَدِّمَة.

Read each guide once, then use Cover answers on this sheet to test yourself.
SG 1 · Lesson 0 · Introductionmust-know facts
  • The unit is based on the book Ta’līm aṣ-Ṣibyān at-Tawḥīd by Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab. The poem (naẓm) is the same book in verse.
  • The poem exists so the content can be memorized more easily.
  • Every answer in the book is given with a dalīl (Qur’an or ḥadīth proof).
  • Al-Fiṭrah is natural — it is not a belief taught from scratch.
  • The goal is understanding — not repeating answers without knowing the dalīl behind them.
SG 2 · Lesson 1 · Q1–Q2 — Who is your Lord?must-know facts
  • Ar-Rabb has six meanings — Creator, Owner, Provider, Helper, Supporter, and the One Worshipped. It does not have just one.
  • Rabb points to Allah’s lordship and His actions. Allah points to His unique right to be worshipped. They are not exact synonyms.
  • Al-Ulūhiyyah is the quality of deserving worship — not merely creating.
  • One proof — Al-A‘rāf 7:54 — answers Q1, Q2 and Q3 together.
  • الشَّهِيد (Witness) is not one of the six meanings.
AMAN · amanschoolmn.orgYouth Educated… Family Cultivated… World IlluminatedE5 Guide · p1/9
Exam 5 Study Guide · Cumulative Mastery · Application — page 2 of 9
SG 3 · Lesson 2 · Q3 — His Signsmust-know facts
  • A sign is what Allah alone does — the sun, moon, earth, sky. Man-made things (a drawing, video game, toy, cartoon) are not signs of Allah.
  • The poem lists five signs: the earth, the sky, the sun, the moon, and the passing hours. Night and day changing is also a sign.
  • Signs are found in creation itself — not only in the Qur’an’s text. The Qur’an describes creation as a proof pointing to the Creator.
  • We do not know Allah only because someone told us — His signs show Him too.
  • Why it matters: it should lead to gratitude, remembrance (dhikr) and worship — not taking creation for granted.
SG 4 · Lesson 3 · Q4 — Purpose & Ibadahmust-know facts
  • The purpose of creation is worship of Allah alone.
  • Q4 has two proofs: Adh-Dhāriyāt 51:56 and An-Nisā’ 4:36. (Al-Ikhlāṣ 112:1 is not one of them.)
  • Ibādah is a comprehensive term for everything Allah loves and is pleased with — far more than the five prayers. This definition is credited to Ibn Taymiyyah.
  • Two conditions for accepted worship — Ikhlāṣ and Mutāba‘ah. A deed needs both together; looking correct outwardly is not enough.
  • Riyā’ ruins sincerity — the deed is no longer purely for Allah, so it can be rejected.
SG 5 · Lesson 4 · Shirk — Definitions & Proofsmust-know facts
  • Shirk = making a nidd for Allah — calling on it, hoping in it, fearing it, relying on it, or having strong desire toward it, besides Allah.
  • Five types of worship where Shirk can occur: Du‘ā, Khawf, Rajā’, Tawakkul, Mahabbah. (Ṣalāh is not on this list.)
  • Khawf becomes Shirk if directed to other than Allah in a controlling way. Rajā’: hoping in a creation the way one hopes in Allah. Tawakkul: relying totally on other than Allah.
  • Full trust in Allah while using permitted means (like studying for a test) is correct Tawakkul — not Shirk.
  • Shirk is the greatest of all sins — not a minor or easily forgivable one.
AMAN · amanschoolmn.orgYouth Educated… Family Cultivated… World IlluminatedE5 Guide · p2/9
Exam 5 Study Guide · Cumulative Mastery · Application — page 3 of 9
SG 6 · Lesson 5 · Taghut — Definition & the First Obligationmust-know facts
  • The definition of Ṭāghūt taught in class is credited to Ibn al-Qayyim. Three categories: something worshipped, followed, or obeyed besides Allah.
  • First obligation on every servant: kufr bi-Ṭāghūt and īmān billāh. Rejecting Ṭāghūt is obligatory for every believer — never optional.
  • An-Naḥl 16:36: every messenger to every nation called: worship Allah and avoid Ṭāghūt.
  • Lā ilāha illa Allāh negates everything false FIRST (لَا إِلَهَ), then affirms Allah (إِلَّا اللَّه) — the same order as kufr bi-Ṭāghūt before īmān billāh.
  • Examples: a Kāhin, a Munajjim, someone obeyed while commanding disobedience to Allah. Modern: horoscopes/fortune-telling, a person or ideology obeyed even in sin, wealth or fame treated as life’s ultimate purpose.
  • Consulting a fortune-teller “just to check” is forbidden and undermines correct worship. A person cannot be a complete believer while following a Ṭāghūt.
SG 7 · Lesson 6 · Q5 — Islam & the Five Pillarsmust-know facts
  • Four components of Islam: (1) submission through Tawḥīd, (2) compliance through obedience, (3) allegiance toward Muslims, (4) rejection of Shirk and its people.
  • Why belief alone is not enough: Islam also requires actual obedience, loyalty to fellow believers, and active rejection of Shirk.
  • Five pillars: Shahādatayn, Ṣalāh, Zakah, Ṣawm, Ḥajj. Zakah is a pillar. Jihad is not one of the five.
  • Hajj is obligatory only on those who are able (physically and financially).
  • Islam is the religion of Allah for ALL His servants — not only Arabs — from the creation of Ādam on.
SG 8 · Lesson 6 · Īmān & the Unseenmust-know facts
  • The six pillars of Īmān: Allah, the Angels, the Books, the Messengers, the Last Day, and Al-Qadar.
  • All six must be believed in together — a person cannot pick and choose. The Five Pillars of Islam are not one of the six.
  • A believer must accept Al-Qadar in both the good and the difficult decree. In the poem, وَالَّذِي كُتِبْ refers to Al-Qadar.
  • Al-Ba‘th is coming back to life after death. Denying it is Kufr — it is one of the six pillars, a foundation, not optional.
  • After being raised, people face Jannah, the Fire, and al-Ḥisāb.
AMAN · amanschoolmn.orgYouth Educated… Family Cultivated… World IlluminatedE5 Guide · p3/9
Exam 5 Study Guide · Cumulative Mastery · Application — page 4 of 9
SG 9 · Lesson 7 · Q6 — The Prophet ﷺmust-know facts
  • Lineage: Muhammad ibn ‘Abdillah ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hāshim ibn ‘Abd Manāf ﷺ. Proof that he is the Seal: Al-Aḥzāb 33:40.
  • He ﷺ was sent to ALL of humanity (الأَحْمَر وَالأَسْوَد), not only the Arabs. There is no prophet after him.
  • Revelation began at 40. He called for 23 years total: 13 in Makkah (3 in secret) and 10 in Madinah. He passed away at 63, after the religion was completed and perfected.
  • The Isrā’ and Mi‘rāj happened before the Hijrah, still in Makkah — the five daily prayers were made obligatory then.
  • Nūḥ was the first messenger (after Shirk appeared). Muhammad ﷺ is the last in time but first in rank.
  • The four rightly-guided caliphs, in order: Abū Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Uthmān, ‘Alī.
  • Best generations: the Ṣaḥābah, then the Tābi‘ūn, then the Followers of the Followers.
  • ‘Eesā will descend near the end of time, break the cross, the swine will be killed — and mankind will accept ONLY Islam.
Proofs (Dalīl) you may be asked for
Al-A‘rāf 7:54
Answers Q1, Q2 and Q3 together — heavens and earth created in six days.
Adh-Dhāriyāt 51:56
“I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Me.”
An-Nisā’ 4:36
Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him.
Al-Mā’idah 5:72
Shirk forbids Jannah; one’s home becomes the Fire.
Al-Jinn 72:18
Mosques are for Allah — do not call on anyone besides Him.
Al-Mu’minūn 23:117
Du‘ā to another deity = Kufr. Such a person will NOT succeed (لَا يُفْلِحُ الْكَافِرُونَ).
Ghāfir 40:60
Du‘ā IS an act of worship.
Az-Zumar 39:64-66
Shirk nullifies ALL good deeds — even hypothetically warning the Prophet ﷺ.

Watch Out — Common Mistakes
The book was written by Ibn al-Qayyim.
Written by Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab.
Sibyān means adult scholars.
Sibyān means children / young boys.
Deeds still benefit a person without Tawḥīd.
Nothing at all benefits a person without Tawḥīd.
Al-Fiṭrah is something taught from scratch.
Al-Fiṭrah is the natural disposition every person is born with.
Some answers in the book come with no proof.
Every answer is given with a dalīl.
Ar-Rabb has only one meaning: Creator.
Ar-Rabb has six meanings.
Common Mistakes (continued)
Rabb and Allāh mean exactly the same thing.
Rabb points to lordship/actions; Allāh to the unique right to be worshipped.
The proof for Q1–Q3 is from Al-Baqarah.
The proof is Al-A‘rāf 7:54.
Al-Ulūhiyyah means being a creator only.
Al-Ulūhiyyah means truly deserving worship.
“Witness” is one of the six meanings of Rabb.
The six are Creator, Owner, Provider, Helper, Supporter, One Worshipped.
A drawing or video game counts as a sign of Allah.
Man-made things are not signs — signs are what Allah alone does.
Signs can only be found in the Qur’an.
Signs are in creation itself, not only the Qur’an’s text.

Exam 5 Study Guide · Cumulative Mastery · Application — page 6 of 9
Common Mistakes (continued)
We know Allah only because someone told us.
We also know Him through His signs and creation.
Ibādah is only the five daily prayers.
Ibādah is everything Allah loves and is pleased with.
The proof for Q4 is only one ayah.
Q4 has two proofs: Adh-Dhāriyāt 51:56 and An-Nisā’ 4:36.
A deed is accepted even without sincerity if it looks correct.
A deed needs sincerity AND following the Prophet ﷺ.
Riyā’ strengthens sincerity.
Riyā’ ruins sincerity.
One of the two conditions is enough.
Both conditions are needed together.
Common Mistakes (continued)
Shirk is a minor, easily forgivable sin.
Shirk is the greatest of all sins.
Al-Mu’minūn 23:117 says calling on another deity leads to success.
Such a person will NOT succeed.
Khawf can never become Shirk.
Khawf CAN become Shirk if directed to other than Allah in a controlling way.
Trusting Allah while studying for a test is Shirk.
Using permitted means with trust in Allah is correct Tawakkul.
The first obligation is belief in Allah, before disbelief in Ṭāghūt.
Kufr bi-Ṭāghūt comes first (then īmān billāh).
A person can be a complete believer while following a Ṭāghūt.
He cannot.
Common Mistakes (continued)
Rejecting Ṭāghūt is optional for a “strong enough” believer.
It is obligatory for every believer.
You can worship Allah correctly and still visit a fortune-teller “just to check.”
That is forbidden and undermines correct worship.
Islam has only two components.
Islam has FOUR components.
Zakah is not one of the five pillars.
Zakah IS a pillar.
Hajj is obligatory on every Muslim regardless of ability.
Hajj is only for those who are able.
Islam is only for Arabs.
Islam is Allah’s religion for ALL His servants.

Common Mistakes (continued)
Al-Qadar only needs to be believed in when the decree is good.
Both the good and the difficult decree.
A person can pick and choose which pillars to believe in.
All six must be believed in together.
The Five Pillars of Islam are one of the six pillars of Īmān.
They are not — the six are Allah, Angels, Books, Messengers, Last Day, Al-Qadar.
Khātam an-Nabiyyīn means the first of the prophets.
It means the Seal (last) of the prophets.
The Prophet ﷺ was sent only to the Arabs.
He ﷺ was sent to all of humanity.
The Isrā’ and Mi‘rāj happened after the Hijrah.
They happened before the Hijrah, in Makkah.
Common Mistakes (continued)
After ‘Eesā’s return mankind will accept other religions.
Mankind will accept ONLY Islam.
Applying What You KnowExam 5 gives you new situations
  • Name the idea first (Rabb, Ilāh, Shirk, Taghut, Iman…), then match it to the situation.
  • Give the proof when you can — the dalīl is what turns an opinion into an answer.
  • Ask: is this worship (Ibadah) directed to Allah alone, or to something else?
  • Use the exact terms from the guides; a correct idea in loose words earns less.

Exam 1 — Midterm (Lessons 0-4)
Part A (True / False): 1-T · 2-T · 3-T · 4-T · 5-T · 6-F (Written by Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab, not Ibn al-Qayyim.) · 7-F (Ar-Rabb has six meanings: Creator, Owner, Provider, Helper, Supporter, and the One Worshipped.) · 8-T · 9-F (Q4 has TWO proofs: Adh-Dhāriyāt 51:56 and An-Nisā’ 4:36.) · 10-F (Shirk is the greatest of all sins, not a minor or easily forgivable one.) · 11-F (The poem says nothing at all benefits a person without Tawhid.) · 12-T · 13-F (Man-made things are not signs of Allah — signs are what Allah alone does (sun, moon, earth, sky).) · 14-T · 15-T · 16-T · 17-T · 18-T · 19-T · 20-T · 21-F (Al-Fiṭrah IS the natural disposition every person is born with — it is not taught from scratch.) · 22-T · 23-T · 24-F (Al-‘Ibādah is a comprehensive term for everything Allah loves and is pleased with — far more than the five prayers.) · 25-T · 26-T · 27-F (The proof (for Q1, Q2, and Q3 together) is Al-A‘rāf 7:54, not Al-Baqarah.) · 28-F (Signs are found in creation itself (the sun, moon, earth, sky), not only in the Qur’an’s text.) · 29-T · 30-T · 31-T · 32-T · 33-T · 34-T · 35-F (It says such a person will NOT succeed (لَا يُفْلِحُ الْكَافِرُونَ).) · 36-F (Every answer is given WITH a dalīl (Qur’an/ḥadīth proof).) · 37-T · 38-F (A deed needs BOTH sincerity (Ikhlāṣ) AND following the Prophet ﷺ — outward correctness alone is not enough.) · 39-T · 40-T · 41-F (Al-Ulūhiyyah means the quality of truly deserving worship, not merely creating.) · 42-T
Part B (Multiple Choice): 43-C · 44-D
Part C (Essay): 45-Look for correct use of Rabb/Uluhiyyah, Ibadah, Shirk, Ikhlas/Mutaba‘ah, and a coherent thread connecting them.
Full: Traces Lord → knowing Him via signs → purpose is worship → Shirk ruins that purpose, using 4+ key terms correctly and showing how each step builds on the last.Partial: Names most of the steps and terms, but the logical connections between them are weak or a step is skipped.Minimal: Lists disconnected facts without showing the logical progression, or uses fewer than 2 key terms correctly.
· 46-Correct belief about Allah as sole Rabb and sole possessor of Uluhiyyah should be what drives sincere worship of Him alone.
Full: Explains both conditions clearly with a concrete example showing how a deed fails without one of them.Partial: Explains the concepts but the example is weak or missing.Minimal: Vague, no real example, conditions not clearly connected.

Part E (Short Answer): 41-Submission through Tawhid; Compliance through obedience; Allegiance toward Muslims; Rejection of Shirk/its people.
Full: All four named correctly (submission/Tawḥīd, compliance/obedience, allegiance, rejection of Shirk).Partial: Two or three named correctly.Minimal: Zero or one named correctly.
· 42-Because Islam requires more than internal submission — it also requires actual obedience (compliance), loyalty to fellow believers, and active rejection of Shirk and its people.
Full: Explains belief/submission is only one of four components; names obedience, allegiance, and rejection of Shirk as also required.Partial: States belief alone isn't enough, without naming the other components.Minimal: Vague or unrelated.

Part F (Essay): 43-The bracelet has no power on its own — believing so is Shirk in Tawakkul. Correct: rely on Allah alone.
Full: Identifies this as Shirk in Tawakkul (relying on the bracelet itself) and explains the correct alternative — using permitted means while relying on Allah alone.Partial: Identifies it as Shirk but does not fully explain the correct alternative.Minimal: Does not identify it as Shirk, or the explanation is incorrect.
· 44-No — Iman requires believing in all six pillars, including the Last Day.
Full: Explains this is Kufr since belief in the Last Day is one of the six pillars of Īmān — partial belief is not complete Īmān.Partial: Says it's a problem without clearly connecting to the six pillars.Minimal: Says this is acceptable, or gives no real explanation.
· 45-Grade holistically — accurate quotation, correct concept identification, genuine reflection.
Full: Selects three genuine, correctly-quoted couplets with an accurate concept explanation for each, plus a real reason memorization matters.Partial: Two of three couplets/explanations are accurate; one is weak, misquoted, or unclear.Minimal: Fewer than two accurate couplet-and-explanation pairs.

⚠️ TEACHER REFERENCE — for planning, accreditation, and balance review

This table maps all 55 assessment items to their lesson focus, question-type mix, and predominant cognitive level (Bloom's-style: Recall/Comprehension vs. Application). True/False items throughout the package now require a written correction when False, which raises them from pure recall toward comprehension.

Balance Note

11 items rely on True/False alone with no Multiple Choice, Fill-in-the-Blank, or Short Answer mix — flagged below in gold. These are valid recall checks, but none currently reach the Application level on their own: CW 9, CW 10, CW 11, CW 12, HW 11, QZ 9, TS 6, TS 7, TS 8, TS 9, EX 3. Worth pairing each with its companion item (e.g. CW 9 with QZ 7, which covers the same lesson with a fuller mix) rather than assigning alone when application-level evidence is wanted.
